title: A nonstandard statistics for strongly correlated systems: Two simple examples
authors: Józef Spałek, Piotr Kuterba, Mateusz Wójcik, Danuta Goc-Jagło, Maciej Fidrysiak, Leszek Spałek, Włodzimierz Wójcik
abstract: We discuss two different cases of strongly correlated fermions statistics. The first of them is the non-Fermi liquid (NFL) case, $i.e.$, that of fermions with exclusion of doubly occupancy of quasimomentum states $\{\bf k\}$ with opposite spins ($\uparrow\downarrow$). The second is that of statistical spin liquid (SSL) case, in which the fermion spins hop around and mix with the holes (unoccupied) states. For both cases we calculate the system entropy and the corresponding statistical distribution function, analyzed for a two-dimensional square-lattice filling $n\in [0,1]$ and relative temperature $k_B T/|t|$, where $t<0$ is the nearest neighbor hopping integral. We are particularly interested in the situation when the system of itinerant fermions reduce to the Mott-insulator state for the half-filled band ($n\to1$). This limiting situation signals a qualitative difference between the present SSL statistics and that of uncorrelated fermions representing normal Fermi-liquid state.
summary: This paper introduces and compares three statistical frameworks—Fermi-Dirac, Non-Fermi Liquid (NFL), and Statistical Spin Liquid (SSL)—to describe fermions in correlated lattice models. The key finding is that the SSL statistics provide a physically consistent description of the Mott insulator state by predicting a finite entropy, suggesting a fundamental change in carrier nature at this quantum critical point.
main_problem: The paper develops nonstandard statistical descriptions for strongly correlated fermionic systems that go beyond standard Fermi-liquid theory.
main_result: It shows that the Statistical Spin Liquid (SSL) statistics correctly predicts a finite, non-zero entropy in the Mott insulating limit ($n 	o 1$), contrasting with predictions from both Fermi-Dirac and Non-Fermi Liquid models.
method: The authors calculate system entropy and statistical distribution functions by deriving generalized counting principles that incorporate specific state exclusions for different correlated regimes (NFL vs. SSL).
model_or_system: The study analyzes strongly correlated fermions on a two-dimensional square lattice, modeled using concepts derived from Hubbard lattice models, characterized by filling $n \in [0, 1]$.
key_observables: System entropy ($S$), statistical distribution function ($n_{k\sigma}$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
important_parameters: Band filling $n \in [0, 1]$, relative temperature $k_B T/|t|$, and the Mott-insulator limit ($n 	o 1$).
main_assumptions: The SSL formulation assumes a two-fluid system with distinguishable spin subsystems ($\uparrow$ and $\downarrow$) in general situations.
figures_summary: Figures compare $n_k$ vs. energy for FD, NFL, and SSL; they also plot entropy ($S$) vs. filling ($n$), and chemical potential ($\mu$) vs. filling ($n$) across the different statistical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares three statistics (FD, NFL, SSL) by calculating their respective entropies and distribution functions for a 2D lattice system, paying special attention to the behavior near the Mott insulator transition.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter theory, the concept of 'transmutation of statistics' as the system crosses a quantum critical point (Mott transition) is highly relevant to understanding emergent collective behaviors in strongly interacting many-body systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overall behavior of the statistical distribution function nk as a function of relative particle energy xk ≡(ϵk −µ)/kBT for three cases: Fermi-Dirac (FD, blue line), non-Fermi liquid (NFL, red), and statistical spin liquid (SSL). For detailed explanation see main text.

Fig. 2. Entropy versus band filling n for the three statistics: FD, NFL, and SSL for the two temperatures kBT/|t|: 10 and 1. Note that for n →1, the entropy reaches the local-moment limit ln 2 for SSL, whereas the corresponding high-temperature limit in the FD cases is 2 ln 2, and for NFL S →0.

Fig. 3. Entropy versus temperature for the two band fillings, n = 0.80 (a) and 0.99 (b). For n →1 the full local moment is recovered only in SSL case, a clear sign of the statistics changeover from that of itinerant (indistinguishable particles) to that of local character (distinguishable spins) in k-space.

Fig. 4. Statistical distribution function nk versus quasimomentum k = (kx, 0); i.e., along Γ −X direction in the Brillouin zone (cf. inset). Temperature kBT/|t| = 1 (a) and 0.01 (b). Note that chemical potential position in the NFL and SSL cases touches the zone boundary (kx, π), whereas it is placed at about kx = π/2, as elaborated in the text.

Fig. 5. Distribution functions nk along the kx = ky (Γ −M) direction, for two temperatures specified. The difference between the chemical potential position for NFL and SSL from one side and that for FD is clearly visible, particularly at lower temperature. For elaboration of this difference see main text.
